legalBasis.value: Residence visa for highly qualified activity and residence permit for highly qualified activity (articles 61 and 90 of Lei 23/2007, as amended, latest by Lei 62/2026)

legalMinimumInvestment.value: Article 90 does not set a minimum investment payment. Some private providers sell packages that include company and research-project services; their price and scope are provider-specific.

packagePriceReported.value: About €170,000 to €200,000, often quoted at €175,000, reported by providers, October 2026. No government body sets or checks these prices.
packagePriceReported.source: Provider websites, October 2026; not set or checked by any government body

absenceLimit.value: A temporary permit may be cancelled after more than 6 consecutive months or 8 non-consecutive months outside Portugal during the permit's total validity without good reason (article 85(2)). It is not cancelled if the holder proves professional, business, cultural or social activity during the absence (article 85(4)). A longer absence should be justified to AIMA before leaving, or afterwards in exceptional cases (article 85(3)). For permanent residence the limits are 24 months in a row, or 30 months in total within 3 years (article 85(2)(b)).

goldenVisaStay.value: Golden Visa holders need at least 7 days in the first year, then 14 days. This lighter rule does not apply to the highly qualified activity permit.

familyReunification.value: These rules apply to applications made after Lei 61/2025 came into force on 23 October 2025. Your filing date can change which rules apply. The 2-year wait (article 98(1)) does not apply to dependent minors or incapacitated members, to a spouse or partner who is the parent or adoptive parent of a dependent minor or incapacitated person, or to families of article 90, 90-A and 121-A holders (article 98(3)). Other exceptional cases may have the wait waived or reduced by ministerial decision (article 98(4)). The marriage or union must be valid and recognised, and both partners must be at least 18 when the application is made. Article 89 families are not in that list, so the 2-year wait (or 15 months for a spouse who lived with the holder for at least 18 months before entry) applies unless one of these exceptions does.

familyDecisionDeadline.value: AIMA must decide within 9 months. For article 90 families the law allows one extension of the same length, but only in exceptional circumstances linked to the complexity of the application, and AIMA must tell you. It is not automatic. We have no official data on how often AIMA uses it (article 105).

familyIntegration.value: Once the family permit is granted, family members must take Portuguese language and constitutional values training, and children must attend compulsory school. Renewal depends on it, with exceptions. This applies to article 90 families too. The practical details are set by a regulatory decree, which we have not yet seen in force (article 101(3) to (5)).

permanentResidence.value: Permanent residence status has no fixed expiry date. The residence card must be renewed every five years, and sooner if a registered identification detail changes (article 76). Article 80 requires 5 years of temporary residence, no sentence or sentences adding up to more than 1 year in prison in the last 5 years, means of subsistence, housing and basic Portuguese.

citizenshipYears.value: 10 years of legal residence for most nationals, 7 years for EU nationals and nationals of countries where Portuguese is an official language. These are minimum residence conditions, not guarantees.

nationalityLawInForce.value: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, published 18 May 2026, in force 19 May 2026

nationalityTransition.value: Applications already pending on 19 May 2026 are decided under the previous rules

languagePresumption.value: For nationals of countries where Portuguese is an official language, the law presumes the Portuguese-language element is met unless lack of Portuguese is manifest. That presumption does not remove the separate requirements concerning Portuguese culture, history, and national symbols.

citizenshipClockStart.value: Not settled. The old rule counting time from the permit application was revoked. Several law firms say time now counts from the first residence card. The law text does not say this expressly.

ificiRate.value: 20% tax on eligible Portuguese work income for 10 years, with most foreign income exempt. Not automatic for highly qualified activity permit holders: it depends on the employer and the role. Each category has its own conditions. Check yours with a Portuguese tax adviser.

ificiDeadline.value: Register by 15 January of the year after becoming tax resident

goldenVisaOptions.value: €500,000 in qualifying investment funds, €500,000 for scientific research, €250,000 for arts and culture, €500,000 company investment with 5 jobs, or creating 10 jobs. Real estate routes closed since 7 October 2023.

goldenVisaRenewal.value: First permit 2 years, then 3-year renewals (article 75). The Golden Visa permit is renewed for 2-year periods (article 90-A(2)).

goldenVisaLowDensity.value: The job-creation, research and arts and culture amounts can be 20% lower in low-density territories, defined by Portaria 208/2017 as under 100 inhabitants per km2 or GDP per head below 75% of the national average. The fund and company routes are not reduced (article 3(2) and (3)).

aimaDecisionDeadline.value: 90 days, extendable by 30 days. This is a legal deadline, not a measured average.

governmentFees.value: AIMA fees changed on 1 March 2026. Exact current amounts not yet confirmed.

residenceWindow.value: All periods of legal residence are added together if they fall within 12 years (9 years for EU nationals and nationals of countries where Portuguese is an official language)

spouseException.value: Under the general 2-year rule, a spouse or partner who lived with the holder for at least 18 months before entry can apply after 15 months

goldenVisaFamilyExempt.value: Family members of article 90-A (Golden Visa) holders are exempt from the 2-year family reunification wait

residenceVisaValidity.value: The D3 residence visa allows two entries and a stay of up to 4 months (article 58(2))

iasMonthly2026.value: IAS (social support index) is €537.13 a month in 2026

techVisaQualification.value: The Tech Visa programme (Portaria 328/2018) looks for an ISCED 2011 level 6 qualification, or level 5 with five years' experience in specialised technical functions. Education is one of several conditions.

naturalisationCriminalBar.value: A final conviction with an effective prison sentence of more than 3 years for certain serious crimes blocks naturalisation

constitutionalCourtRuling.value: On 15 December 2025 an earlier draft of the nationality law was partly struck down. That event is history. It is not support for any current rule.

familyPermitDuration.value: It runs for the same length as the main applicant's permit (article 107(1) of Lei 23/2007). After 2 years, or earlier in some cases, family members can get their own permit (article 107(3) and (4)).

feie2026.value: US foreign earned income exclusion is up to $132,900 for 2026
